prompt:
Consider $x + y + z = 2$, $2x + 3y + z = 5$, $x + 3y - z = k$.

**(a)** Find the value of $k$ for which the system has infinitely many solutions. **[4]**

**(b)** For this value of $k$, find the general solution. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** R2 − 2R1: $y - z = 1$ (M1)(A1). R3 − R1: $2y - 2z = k - 2$ (A1). Consistent when $k - 2 = 2$, so $k = 4$ (A1)

**(b)** Let $z = \lambda$: $y = 1 + \lambda$, $x = 1 - 2\lambda$ (M1)(A1)
